_note: Diplomacy (docs/diplomacy-design.md, approved; war-and-realm §0.2 overrides: envoys reach anyone, trade continues during war with tariffs, betrayal stays as the V1 rule flagged as the future Chaos trigger). Every number is a PLACEHOLDER for tuning.

envoys._note: Envoys travel automatically by map distance between capitals at metres_per_turn (at least one turn); contact happens on arrival (war-and-realm §0.2).

attitude._note: Attitude events (diplomacy-design §3.3): value and decay per turn toward 0 (0 = permanent). gold_per_point converts attitude into the gold the AI values it at. Faces: five steps by attitude.

prejudice._note: Permanent prejudice (diplomacy-design §3.5): by culture pairs, both ways. The exceptions are factions that seek friendship instead (the Redhand Warband).

blocs._note: Order, Destruction and neutral peoples (game-design §8.7): same-bloc deals +same, cross-bloc deals cross (in attitude-equivalent points) and cost the proposer cross_reputation with its own bloc.

trust._note: Treaty items are valued x trust, from the receiver's perceived Trustworthy/Treacherous axis: from low (at -100) to high (at +100).

values._note: AI valuation in gold equivalents (diplomacy-design §6). region_turns: a region is worth its income x this; tribute_factor: per-turn gold valued at amount x turns x this x trust; marriage, embassy, nap and access in attitude points; alliance and defensive pacts by the proposer's power relative to the receiver's own (protection) minus the risk of its wars; peace and ceasefire by the war's balance and weariness; vassalage by the power gap and threat. proud and expansionist factions dislike giving land or tribute (x reluctance), generous ones give gold cheaply (x generous).

trade._note: A trade agreement gives both partners share of the partner's settlement income (capped at cap_share of their own), x tariff while at war (war-and-realm §7.3: trade continues during war unless cancelled).

war._note: Declarations (diplomacy-design §7): without a justification the declarer takes the unjustified_war deed and the victim's allies the unprovoked_ally attitude. Minor factions without a protector need no justification and anger only themselves (§13). Weariness grows per turn at war and with losses, decays at peace, and raises the value of peace.
war._outcome_note: Peace by the war's outcome (owner spec 2026-10-07): outcome_swing is the power swing that counts as winning or losing; a winning receiver values peace at winning_refuses (it wants land, gold or fealty), a losing one at losing_accepts; an even war is worth stalemate_value once it is stalemate_turns old.

calls._note: Calls to arms: an ally at war asks for help; each ally joins, supports (support_gold to the caller, -5 with the enemy) or refuses (-15 with the caller). join_at: the willingness needed to join, support_at to support. Treacherous allies x treacherous_factor.

orders._note: Commandable allies and vassals (diplomacy-design §8): willingness from dominance (your strength over theirs), dependence (vassals), rewards (gold offered, per 500 gold), attitude and reputation. An accepted order commits at least min_commit of the target's defence, or the strongest army, never a token force; otherwise it is declined with the reason. Orders expire after expire turns.

ai._note: AI diplomacy: each AI faction thinks every think_every turns (staggered by faction), proposes at most one deal to the player per turn (diplomacy-design §15) and only deals scoring at least accept_margin for itself.
ai._peace_note: An AI faction sues for peace only after peace_min_turns of war (Varos marches take several turns; earlier peace ended most wars before a battle), and then when weariness reaches peace_weariness or the enemy is peace_losing_ratio times stronger.

replies._note: Reply pop-ups (owner spec 2026-10-07): the answering ruler's line, by tone (their attitude toward you: warm at warm_at or more, cordial at cordial_at, hostile at hostile_at or less, else cool) and outcome. {us} is their house, {you} yours, {reason} their objection. Placeholder lines.

warm: Gladly, friend. {us} remembers who stands with it.
Done, and done gladly. May our houses prosper together.
cordial: Agreed. {us} sees the sense in it.
Your terms are fair. We accept.
cool: We accept, for now. Do not mistake this for friendship.
Very well. {us} will hold you to every word.
hostile: We accept, because it suits us. Nothing more.
Take it, then. But {us} forgets nothing.

warm: Forgive us, old friend, we cannot: {reason}.
Not this, not now: {reason}. Ask us again in better times.

embassy.accept: Your people may stay at our court. Mind your manners.
embassy.decline: We will not receive your people: {reason}.

contact.accept: Your envoy has reached us. {us} knows your name now.
